cards.text: Elisha, the prophet known as the man of God, once brought a woman's son back to life (2 Kings 4:32-37). Now he has a word for her from the LORD. Something is coming to the land, and she needs to hear it.

cards.question: Elisha warns the woman that the LORD has decreed a seven-year ___ will come to the land.
With seven hard years coming, what does Elisha tell the woman and her household to do?

answers.text: Leave and live as foreigners wherever they can
Stay home and store up all the grain they can
Move inside the walls of Samaria and wait it out

cards.text: She does exactly as the man of God said and takes her whole household with her. Meanwhile, my alarm tells me one thing and I hit snooze THREE times.

cards.question: The woman and her household live through the famine years in the land of the Philistines.

cards.text: Seven years go by, just like the LORD said. Then the woman brings her household back home from the land of the Philistines.

cards.question: When she gets back, the woman goes to the ___ to make an appeal.
After seven years away, the woman appeals to the king for her house and her land.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the king is talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God. And the king has a request.

cards.question: What does the king ask Gehazi, Elisha's servant, to tell him?

answers.text: All the great things Elisha has done
Where Elisha has been staying lately
Why the famine lasted so many years

cards.question: Out of all of Elisha's great things, which one is Gehazi telling the king about?

answers.text: How Elisha brought the dead back to life
How Elisha split the waters of the Jordan
How Elisha made an iron axhead float

cards.question: Gehazi is right in the middle of that story when the woman comes in to appeal to the king.

cards.text: Gehazi is mid-story about this woman, and she walks right in. Friend, I've been baking for YEARS and I still can't get my cookies and my timer to finish at the same time.

cards.question: Gehazi points out the woman to the king, and he also points out her ___.
When the king asks the woman about it, she tells him Gehazi got the story mixed up.

cards.text: She confirms it, so now the king has heard it from the servant AND from the woman herself. So the king appoints an officer for her.

cards.question: What does the king tell the officer to do for the woman?

answers.text: Give back all that was hers plus all the field produced
Give back her house but keep her field for the crown
Give her a different field close to the king's palace

cards.text: Not just her house and land, but everything that field produced from the day she left until now. Friend, that's like coming back after seven years and finding out your boss saved every paycheck the WHOLE time.

findings.problem: The opening card says only that something is coming, so the baker cannot reason out whether the answer is famine, war or plague. The blank asks for an unseen word from verse 1 rather than a meaning the baker can work out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Verse 3 says that the woman returned, but the card adds that she brought her household back home. The passage does not state or clearly imply that the household returned with her.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The preceding story card says only that the woman returned. It gives no information about her appeal or her property from which the baker could reason out that she approaches the king, so this blank tests unseen wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question depends on 'that story,' pointing back to card 11 instead of identifying Gehazi's account of Elisha bringing the dead back to life. The earlier card is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The phrases 'about it' and 'the story' never identify what the king asks the woman to confirm. The question needs to supply the context that Gehazi has identified her and the son Elisha restored to life.
